args.missing_values: Only positive-occupancy sites count. Retain unmodeled positions in the declared denominator. Omit missing C-alpha sites from the radius without imputation. findings.text: The sole polypeptide in `_entity_poly_seq` maps to chain A in `_pdbx_poly_seq_scheme`. I matched every declared residue by label entity, chain, sequence position and residue identity to the model’s `_atom_site` rows. Every position has finite coordinates for N, CA, C and O, with a single carbon atom named CA. Water belongs to label chain B despite sharing author chain ID A.

The terminal leucine, arginine and glycine pair have partial Cα occupancies. Each retains coordinates for every required backbone atom. The terminal glycine has both O and a separate OXT. The polymer Cα rows have no alternate locations.

The sole polypeptide in `_entity_poly_seq` maps to chain A in `_pdbx_poly_seq_scheme`. I matched every declared residue by label entity, chain, sequence position and residue identity to the model’s `_atom_site` rows. Every position has finite coordinates for N, CA, C and O, with a single carbon atom named CA. Water belongs to label chain B despite sharing author chain ID A.

The terminal leucine, arginine and glycine pair have partial Cα occupancies. Each retains coordinates for every required backbone atom. The terminal glycine has both O and a separate OXT. The polymer Cα rows have no alternate locations.

I support the label “model-1 Cα radius of gyration covering the entire declared 1UBQ chain A.” The declared denominator is the consecutive sequence from Met1 through Gly76. The radius denominator is the count of Cα sites mapped singly to those same positions. Take the arithmetic centroid, then the square root of the sum of squared distances to the centroid divided by the Cα count. Every Cα has equal weight, including Leu73, Arg74, Gly75 and Gly76. N, C and O decide coverage and carry no weight in the radius. Signed by Codex, numerical interpretation researcher.

The competing observed-subset interpretation predicts a declared position missing a required atom. A missing CA reduces the radius denominator and requires recomputing the centroid over the observed sites. A missing O with its CA retained leaves the Cα count and radius unchanged while failing the complete-chain rule. Report the observed Cα scope, name the position and absent atom, and give four-atom coverage separately. A position-by-position comparison with the declared sequence discriminates cases that can give identical radii.

`_exptl.method` identifies X-ray diffraction. The radius describes the geometry of a single refined crystal model. Partial occupancies limit inference about how uniformly the tail adopts the deposited coordinates. Recomputing this model checks arithmetic. Independent sampling requires a separately acquired dataset. A solution comparison requires solution data under stated conditions and attention to ensemble averaging and scattering weights.

gaps: The original supplies a single crystallographic coordinate model. Between-sample variation and solution compactness remain unmeasured.
The numerical radius in ångströms requires the Lead’s executed coordinate readout. The original coordinate table supplies the position and atom identities for this scope review.

findings.text: I matched each chain A polymer position and monomer in _entity_poly_seq and _pdbx_poly_seq_scheme to the complete _atom_site loop for the requested model and entity. Every declared position has exactly one N, CA, C and O with numeric coordinates and full occupancy. The polymer rows all carry the alternate-site marker '.'. Both termini meet the same criterion, and the terminal glycine carbonyl oxygen is explicitly labeled O.
The OH and HEM coordinate rows share the polymer's author chain identifier A. Their label chain and entity identifiers assign them to separate nonpolymer entities, and their label_seq_id is '.'.

The mmCIF and the same-deposition PDB extract flag wrong chirality at a glutamine Cα. The mmCIF validation record describes planar geometry at that atom. Its coordinate row and those for the other required backbone atoms are present at full occupancy.

Source row audit for PDB 1MBN, model 1, label_asym_id A, label_entity_id 1. The declaration and chain scheme run from Val1 to Gly153 inclusive. Checking all _atom_site IDs 1–1260 gives 153 of 153 Cα sites and 612 of 612 required N, CA, C and O sites matched by label sequence position and monomer. All polymer rows, IDs 1–1216, carry occupancy 1.00 and label_alt_id '.'. There are no gaps, zero-occupancy polymer sites or alternate polymer sites.

In N, CA, C, O order, _atom_site.id values are 1, 2, 3, 4 for Val A 1 and 1213, 1214, 1215, 1216 for Gly A 153. OH is ID 1217, label chain B, entity 2, author A 154. HEM spans IDs 1218–1260, label chain C, entity 3, author A 155.

Gln A 8 has _atom_site IDs 58, 59, 60, 61 for N, CA, C, O, each with occupancy 1.00. The mmCIF _database_PDB_caveat.text and the extract's CAVEAT identify Gln A 8 CA. The _pdbx_validate_chiral record lists model 1 and gives details as PLANAR. EXPDTA and REMARK 2 in the same-deposition extract identify X-ray diffraction at 2.00 Å resolution.

The whole-declared-chain coverage label is justified for the model-1 Cα radius. A viewer can interpret the radius as the spatial spread of the deposited Cα trace from Val1 through Gly153. The Gln8 caveat concerns the local geometry at an occupied Cα.
